text: Code refactoring means improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When code is messy, developers waste time trying to figure it out. Refactoring helps fix this problem. It also reduces technical debt, which builds up when teams take shortcuts. For example, you might rename unclear variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. The behavior of the program stays the same, so users do not notice anything different. Regular refactoring keeps a project healthy and makes future changes faster and safer.
